I have resolved the issue where email messages crashed when using non-ASCII hostnames and non-unicode email encoding.

### Root Cause
When the machine hostname contains non-ASCII characters (e.g. `"正宗"` or `"漢字"`), `socket.getfqdn()` returns non-ASCII domain names. When generating default `Message-ID` headers with `make_msgid(domain=DNS_NAME)`, non-ASCII domain names were inserted unencoded into the `Message-ID` header. If the email message encoding was non-unicode (such as `iso-8859-1`), header encoding failed with a `UnicodeEncodeError`.

### Fix
1. In [`CachedDnsName.get_fqdn()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-h0mx60la/django/core/mail/utils.py#L14-L21), converted non-ASCII FQDN hostnames to punycode IDNA (`encode('idna').decode('ascii')`).
2. In [`EmailMessage.message()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-h0mx60la/django/core/mail/message.py#L257-L265), ensured the domain passed to `make_msgid` is encoded using IDNA punycode if non-ASCII.
